Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

npmerger 0.0.0.9000

  • Matched comparison samples:

    • get_panel() builds the full 990 / 990-EZ organization-year panel for every filer, with constant-dollar size, margin, equity ratio, months of cash, NTEE, and subsection (panel_measures(), real_dollars(), cpi_u(), ntee_level()).
    • merger_sample() keeps merger cases whose recipient filed in every year t-2..t+2, with t-3/t-2 baselines for donor and recipient.
    • match_pool() builds eligible comparison org-years: a full t-2..t+2 window around any year, and no Schedule N involvement nearby (schedule_n_events()).
    • match_candidates() finds every candidate in the same NTEE group within size and profitability (or fiscal-health) calipers, across any years, ranked by distance. match_balance() reports standardized differences.
    • dev/build-matching.R adds these tables to the database.

  • Classifier rules revised after hand validation on 300 filings (dev/validation/; PLAN.md section 9). Agreement with hand labels rose from 62% to 70%, and merger recall from 51% to 71%.

    • merger_rules(min_top_share = 0.75): the default was 0.5. The share test now always applies, not only when there are several nonprofit recipients.
    • merger_rules(final_as_termination = TRUE): Part-II-only filings with the final-return box are treated as terminations. New TERMINATED column.
    • merger_rules(sn_text = TRUE): merger language in Schedule N’s own text (SN_MERGER_TEXT from sn_filings(), pattern sn_merger_pattern()) is merger evidence on its own, with BASIS = "sn_text".
    • merger_rules(promote = FALSE) is now the default. Only 1 of 13 promoted filings read as a merger. Set promote = TRUE for a broad definition.

  • build_merger_data() runs the whole pipeline and returns every table. It accepts pre-fetched inputs, so npmerger_example() runs offline.

  • Merger cases: build_merger_cases() (merger IDs, groups, and the merger year on each organization’s fiscal calendar), merger_roles(), transfer_value() (FMV by asset class, coverage of the donor’s assets, outlier flags), and asset_class().

  • Core data: get_core(), org_years() (one return per organization-year), and merger_measures() (harmonized 990 / 990-EZ revenue, expenses, assets, debt, staff costs, executive pay, grants, and overhead). get_bmf() adds NTEE codes and ruling years.

  • Analysis tables: merger_attributes() (donor and recipient attributes with five years of size history), merger_part7() (Part VII rosters from t-2 to t+2 with IN_BOTH), and merger_fiscal_panel() (measures, ‘fiscal’ ratios, an optional fixed-calibration index, and optional trailing smoothing via smooth_trailing()).

  • recover_recipient_ein() recovers missing recipient EINs by unique name and ZIP or state match against 990 filers (get_name_index()).

  • Merger evidence: get_evidence_tables() reads the 990 header, Part VII, Part VI, Schedule O, Schedule R, Schedule A, and mission tables for the donors and recipients in a set of filings. merger_features() adds: Part VII leadership overlap (leader_overlap()), counts of dissolving donors sharing a successor (add_donor_counts()), donor and recipient filing history and new-entity detection (add_filing_history()), corroborating disclosures (add_corroboration()), affiliation (add_affiliation()), and mission similarity (add_mission_similarity()).

  • classify_transactions() can promote an asset transfer to a merger when at least two corroborating signals agree, and records BASIS and N_CORROBORATE.

  • pkgdown site using the NODC pkgstyle template, and an overview vignette.

  • Initial package skeleton: Schedule N retrieval, flag/EIN/IRC-section parsers, transaction-level stacking of Schedule N Parts I and II, merger ID helpers, and default classification rules.

Developed by Jesse Lecy.
